name: Hammurabi
summary: Sixth king of the First Dynasty of Babylon (r. c. 1792–1750 BCE), he turned a small city-state into an empire covering most of Mesopotamia through diplomacy and war against Larsa, Eshnunna and Mari. Late in his reign he set up stone stelae carrying 282 laws, framed as given by the sun god Shamash, so that 'the strong may not oppress the weak'. His letters show a king closely involved in canals, taxes and court cases.

name: Ramesses II
summary: The 'Great Ancestor' of later pharaohs, Ramesses II reigned for 66 years (c. 1279–1213 BCE). He fought the Hittites at Kadesh (c. 1274 BCE), proclaimed it a victory, and later signed the world's oldest surviving peace treaty with them. He built Abu Simbel, the Ramesseum and a new capital, Pi-Ramesses, and fathered over a hundred children.

name: Hatshepsut
known_for: A woman who ruled as king
summary: Daughter of Thutmose I, Hatshepsut ruled first as regent for her stepson Thutmose III and then as pharaoh (c. 1479–1458 BCE), depicted with the royal false beard. Her reign was peaceful and prosperous: she sent an expedition to the land of Punt for incense and built the terraced temple at Deir el-Bahari. After her death her images were chiselled away, perhaps to secure Thutmose III's line.

name: Cyrus the Great
summary: Founder of the Achaemenid Persian Empire (r. c. 559–530 BCE), Cyrus overthrew the Medes, conquered Lydia and took Babylon in 539 BCE almost without a fight. The Cyrus Cylinder records that he returned deported peoples and restored their temples; the Bible praises him for letting the Jews return to Jerusalem. He died campaigning in Central Asia and was buried in a simple tomb at Pasargadae.

name: Alexander the Great
summary: King of Macedon at 20, Alexander (356–323 BCE) was taught by Aristotle and in 11 years conquered the Persian Empire, Egypt and lands to the Indus, never losing a major battle. At the Hydaspes (326 BCE) he defeated Porus, but his exhausted army refused to go beyond the Beas. He founded cities, mixed Greek and Persian elites and spread Greek culture, but died in Babylon at 32, and his empire split among his generals.

name: Chandragupta Maurya
summary: With the guidance of his mentor Chanakya, Chandragupta (r. c. 322–297 BCE) overthrew the Nanda dynasty and founded the Maurya Empire, the first to unite most of the Indian subcontinent. He defeated Seleucus I, who ceded the northwest in exchange for 500 elephants. Jain tradition says he abdicated, became a monk under Bhadrabahu and fasted to death at Shravanabelagola.

name: Ashoka
summary: Grandson of Chandragupta, Ashoka (r. c. 268–232 BCE) conquered Kalinga in a war that his own edict says killed 100,000 and deported 150,000. Filled with remorse, he embraced Buddhism and dhamma — non-violence, tolerance and welfare — building hospitals, wells and rest houses and sending missions abroad. His lion capital at Sarnath is India's national emblem and his wheel is on its flag.

name: Qin Shi Huang
summary: King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six rival Warring States and in 221 BCE proclaimed himself First Emperor. He standardised script, coins, weights and roads, joined border walls into an early Great Wall, and ordered the burning of books and the persecution of scholars. Obsessed with immortality, he died in 210 BCE and was buried with the Terracotta Army.

name: Julius Caesar
summary: A Roman general and politician (100–44 BCE), Caesar conquered Gaul, crossed the Rubicon in 49 BCE to start a civil war, and became dictator. He reformed the calendar (the Julian calendar) and expanded the Senate. Senators who feared he would become king stabbed him on the Ides of March, 44 BCE; his heir Octavian became Rome's first emperor.

name: Augustus
summary: Born Octavian, Caesar's adopted heir defeated Antony and Cleopatra at Actium (31 BCE) and in 27 BCE became Augustus, the first Roman emperor. He kept republican forms while holding real power, began 200 years of the Pax Romana, built roads and temples, and said he found Rome brick and left it marble. The month of August is named after him.

name: Cleopatra
summary: Cleopatra VII (69–30 BCE), last of the Ptolemies and the only one to learn Egyptian, allied with Julius Caesar and then Mark Antony to preserve Egypt's independence. After their defeat at Actium, she took her own life rather than be paraded in Rome. Egypt became a Roman province.

name: Kanishka
summary: The greatest Kushan emperor (r. c. 127–150 CE), Kanishka ruled from Bactria to the Ganga with capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura. A patron of Buddhism, he convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir and supported Gandhara art. His coins show Greek, Persian, Indian and Buddhist gods.

name: Samudragupta
summary: The Gupta emperor (r. c. 335–375 CE) described in the Allahabad pillar inscription as having defeated kings across north India and made southern rulers tributaries. He also performed the horse sacrifice and was depicted on coins playing the veena, showing his love of music and poetry.

name: Justinian I
summary: Byzantine emperor (r. 527–565) who tried to restore the Roman Empire, reconquering North Africa and Italy. He codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis, rebuilt Hagia Sophia, and survived the Nika riots thanks to his wife Theodora. His reign was also struck by the Plague of Justinian.

name: Harsha
summary: Harshavardhana (r. 606–647) unified north India from Kannauj, wrote Sanskrit plays (Ratnavali, Nagananda), and hosted the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang. Pulakeshin II stopped his southern expansion at the Narmada.

name: Charlemagne
summary: King of the Franks (r. 768–814), crowned emperor by Pope Leo III in 800, he united much of western Europe, conquered the Saxons and Lombards, and sponsored the Carolingian Renaissance of learning and script.

name: Rajaraja Chola I
summary: Chola emperor (r. 985–1014) who conquered the Cheras, Pandyas and northern Sri Lanka, built a navy, carried out a land survey, and built the Brihadeeswarar temple at Thanjavur (1010).

name: Genghis Khan
summary: Born Temüjin (c. 1162–1227), he united the Mongol tribes in 1206 and conquered from China to Persia, creating the largest land empire. He used merit-based promotion, a postal system and religious tolerance, but his conquests killed millions.

name: Razia Sultan
known_for: First woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate
summary: The only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate (1236–1240), she wore a man's clothes, led armies and appointed non-Turkic officials, angering nobles who overthrew and killed her.

name: Mansa Musa
known_for: Perhaps the richest person in history
summary: Emperor of Mali (r. c. 1312–1337), perhaps the richest person in history. His hajj in 1324 made Mali famous, and he built mosques and libraries in Timbuktu.

name: Krishnadevaraya
summary: Vijayanagara emperor (r. 1509–1529) who defeated the Deccan sultans and Gajapatis, patronised Telugu and Kannada poets (the Ashtadiggajas) and wrote Amuktamalyada.

name: Babur
summary: A descendant of Timur and Genghis Khan, Babur lost his homeland Fergana, took Kabul, and defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat (1526) with field guns, founding the Mughal Empire. His memoir, the Baburnama, is frank and vivid.

name: Akbar
summary: The greatest Mughal emperor (r. 1556–1605), Akbar expanded the empire across north India, abolished the jizya tax on non-Muslims, married Rajput princesses, held interfaith debates in the Ibadat Khana and created a revenue system under Todar Mal.

name: Shah Jahan
summary: Mughal emperor (r. 1628–1658) who built the Taj Mahal for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, the Red Fort and Jama Masjid in Delhi. His son Aurangzeb imprisoned him in Agra Fort.

name: Elizabeth I
summary: Queen of England (r. 1558–1603), she restored Protestantism, defeated the Spanish Armada and presided over a golden age of literature, including Shakespeare. The East India Company was chartered under her in 1600.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji
known_for: Founded the Maratha state; navy; hill forts
summary: Founder of the Maratha state (1630–1680), Shivaji built hill forts, a navy and an efficient administration, fought Bijapur and the Mughals and was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674.

name: Peter the Great
summary: Tsar of Russia (r. 1682–1725) who travelled incognito to western Europe, modernised the army, built a navy and founded St Petersburg.

name: Maharaja Ranjit Singh
summary: The 'Lion of Punjab' (1780–1839) united Sikh misls and built a strong, secular empire with a modern army.

name: Tipu Sultan
summary: The 'Tiger of Mysore' (1750–1799) fought the British in four wars, used iron rockets and died defending Srirangapatna.

name: Napoleon Bonaparte
summary: French general who became emperor (1804), conquered much of Europe and created the Napoleonic Code, before defeat at Waterloo (1815).

name: Queen Victoria
summary: Queen of the UK (r. 1837–1901) and Empress of India from 1877, whose reign saw industrial and imperial expansion.

name: Rani Lakshmibai
summary: Queen of Jhansi (c. 1828–1858) who fought the British in the 1857 rebellion after they annexed her kingdom under the Doctrine of Lapse, and died in battle at Gwalior.

name: Mangal Pandey
summary: A sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry who attacked his officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857; his execution helped spark the rebellion.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
summary: Mohandas Gandhi (1869–1948) developed satyagraha (non-violent resistance) in South Africa and led India's freedom movement through the Non-Cooperation, Salt March and Quit India campaigns. He was assassinated in 1948.

name: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: India's first Prime Minister (1947–1964), he built democratic institutions, planned industry, scientific institutes, and led the Non-Aligned Movement.

name: B. R. Ambedkar
known_for: Chief architect of the Constitution; fought caste
summary: A Dalit scholar (1891–1956) with doctorates from Columbia and LSE, he chaired the Constituent Assembly's drafting committee and fought caste discrimination.

name: Subhas Chandra Bose
summary: A Congress president (1938–39) who led the Indian National Army with Japanese support to fight British rule.

name: Bhagat Singh
summary: A revolutionary (1907–1931) hanged at 23 for shooting a British officer; his writings argued for socialism.

name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
summary: India's first Home Minister, he integrated over 560 princely states into India.

name: Sarojini Naidu
summary: Poet and freedom fighter, first Indian woman president of Congress (1925).

name: Birsa Munda
known_for: Ulgulan rebellion for tribal land rights
summary: A tribal leader (1875–1900) who led the Ulgulan against British and landlords.

name: Nelson Mandela
summary: Anti-apartheid leader imprisoned for 27 years who became South Africa's first black president (1994).

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
summary: Civil rights leader who used non-violent protest inspired by Gandhi.

name: Winston Churchill
summary: Opposed Indian independence.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
summary: US president during the Depression and WWII.

name: Adolf Hitler
summary: Nazi dictator who started WWII and the Holocaust.

name: Joseph Stalin
summary: Soviet dictator whose purges and famines killed millions.

name: Mao Zedong
summary: The Great Leap Forward famine killed tens of millions.

name: Confucius
summary: Kong Fuzi (551–479 BCE) taught ethics, family loyalty, ritual and good government; his sayings were compiled as the Analects and became China's state philosophy under the Han.

name: Laozi
summary: Traditional author of the Daodejing, founder of Taoism, teaching harmony with the Dao and non-action (wu wei).

name: Gautama Buddha
summary: Siddhartha Gautama, a Shakya prince, left home to seek an end to suffering, attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, and taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path for 45 years.

name: Mahavira
summary: The 24th Jain tirthankara taught non-violence (ahimsa), truthfulness and non-attachment.

name: Socrates
summary: Athenian philosopher who questioned everything; executed in 399 BCE.

name: Plato
summary: Student of Socrates who founded the Academy and wrote the Republic.

name: Aristotle
summary: Plato's student and Alexander's tutor; founded logic and biology.

name: Chanakya
summary: Kautilya, the Brahmin strategist who helped Chandragupta overthrow the Nandas; traditionally credited with the Arthashastra.

name: Panini
summary: Grammarian of Gandhara (c. 4th century BCE) whose Ashtadhyayi described Sanskrit in about 4,000 rules, a precursor of formal linguistics and computing.

name: Archimedes
summary: Greek mathematician of Syracuse who calculated π, discovered buoyancy and designed war machines.

name: Sushruta
summary: Ancient Indian surgeon whose Sushruta Samhita describes plastic surgery and over 300 procedures.

name: Charaka
summary: Physician whose Charaka Samhita is a foundation of Ayurveda.

name: Thiruvalluvar
summary: Tamil poet who wrote the Tirukkural, 1,330 couplets on ethics, wealth and love.

name: Aryabhata
summary: Mathematician (476–550 CE) who in the Aryabhatiya calculated π to 3.1416, said the Earth rotates, and explained eclipses.

name: Kalidasa
summary: The greatest classical Sanskrit poet and playwright, author of Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta.

name: Brahmagupta
summary: Mathematician (598–668) who gave rules for calculating with zero and negative numbers.

name: Adi Shankaracharya
summary: Philosopher who taught Advaita Vedanta and founded four mathas.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
summary: Baghdad scholar whose works gave 'algebra' and 'algorithm' and spread Indian numerals.

name: Ibn Sina (Avicenna)
summary: Persian physician and philosopher, author of the Canon of Medicine.

name: Al-Biruni
summary: Scholar who wrote Kitab al-Hind on Indian science and religion.

name: Bhaskara II
summary: Mathematician whose Lilavati and Siddhanta Shiromani anticipated ideas of calculus.

name: Ibn Battuta
summary: Moroccan traveller who covered 120,000 km.

name: Kabir
summary: Weaver-poet who criticised caste and ritual in Hindu and Muslim religion.

name: Guru Nanak
summary: Founder of Sikhism who taught one God, equality and service.

name: Mirabai
summary: Rajput princess and Krishna devotee whose songs defied convention.

name: Leonardo da Vinci
summary: Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa and inventor.

name: Nicolaus Copernicus
summary: Sparked the Scientific Revolution.

name: Galileo Galilei
summary: Used the telescope to support Copernicus; tried by the Inquisition.

name: Isaac Newton
summary: Formulated the laws of motion and gravity.

name: Charles Darwin
summary: Proposed evolution by natural selection.

name: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
summary: Reformer who campaigned against sati and founded the Brahmo Samaj.

name: Savitribai Phule
summary: India's first woman teacher, who opened girls' schools with Jyotirao Phule.

name: Swami Vivekananda
summary: Introduced Vedanta to the West at Chicago (1893).

name: Rabindranath Tagore
summary: First non-European Nobel laureate in literature (1913).

name: Marie Curie
summary: First person to win two Nobel prizes.

name: Albert Einstein
summary: Developed relativity.

name: C. V. Raman
summary: National Science Day marks his discovery.

name: Srinivasa Ramanujan
summary: Self-taught genius at Cambridge.

name: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
summary: Missile scientist and President of India.

name: Sargon of Akkad
summary: Born, legend says, to a priestess who set him adrift in a reed basket, Sargon rose from cupbearer to king of Kish and conquered the Sumerian cities, uniting Mesopotamia from the Gulf to Syria. He installed his daughter Enheduanna as high priestess at Ur; she is the earliest author known by name.

name: Enheduanna
summary: Daughter of Sargon, she served as high priestess of the moon god Nanna at Ur and composed hymns to Inanna, including the Exaltation of Inanna, which were copied for centuries.

name: Imhotep
summary: Chancellor to King Djoser, he designed the Step Pyramid at Saqqara, the first large stone building; later Egyptians worshipped him as a god of medicine.

name: Akhenaten
known_for: Tried to make Egypt worship one sun god
summary: He replaced Egypt's gods with the Aten, built a new capital at Amarna and encouraged a naturalistic art style; after his death his reforms were erased, and his son Tutankhamun restored the old gods.

name: Zoroaster
summary: He taught that the world is a struggle between Ahura Mazda (good) and Angra Mainyu (evil), and that humans choose through good thoughts, words and deeds; his hymns (Gathas) are in the Avesta.

name: Bimbisara
summary: He expanded Magadha through marriage and conquest and was a patron of the Buddha.

name: Pericles
known_for: Led Athens in its golden age
summary: He built the Parthenon and championed democracy; his funeral oration praised Athenian freedom. He died in the plague of Athens.

name: Herodotus
summary: His Histories investigated the Persian Wars and the customs of Egyptians, Scythians and Persians, gathering evidence by travel and interviews.

name: Hippocrates
summary: He taught that diseases have natural causes; the Hippocratic Oath bears his name.

name: Sun Tzu
summary: His treatise on strategy, deception and knowing your enemy is still studied by militaries and businesses.

name: Hannibal
summary: He invaded Italy in 218 BCE and destroyed Roman armies at Cannae (216 BCE), but Rome survived; he was defeated by Scipio at Zama (202 BCE).

name: Euclid
summary: His Elements organised geometry from axioms and proofs and was used as a textbook for over 2,000 years.

name: Sima Qian
summary: He wrote China's first comprehensive history, covering 2,000 years, after enduring castration as punishment rather than suicide.

name: Jesus of Nazareth
summary: A Jewish preacher who taught love of God and neighbour and the coming Kingdom of God, he was crucified under Pontius Pilate; his followers proclaimed his resurrection.

name: Prophet Muhammad
summary: Muslims believe the Quran was revealed to him from 610; he migrated to Medina (622) and united Arabia.

name: Empress Wu Zetian
summary: She ruled as emperor of her own Zhou dynasty (690–705), promoting examinations and Buddhism.

name: Xuanzang
summary: He travelled to India (629–645), studied at Nalanda, and brought 657 texts back to China; his account is a key source on Harsha's India.

name: Ramanuja
summary: He taught qualified non-dualism and devotion to Vishnu, opening temple worship to wider castes.

name: Basava
summary: Minister and poet who rejected caste and ritual, founding the Anubhava Mantapa assembly.

name: Rani Rudramadevi
summary: She ruled in her own right and defended her kingdom.

name: Amir Khusrau
summary: He wrote in Persian and Hindavi.

name: Ibn Khaldun
summary: He studied why dynasties rise and fall through group solidarity (asabiyyah).

name: Zheng He
summary: He led seven fleets to Asia and Africa.

name: Joan of Arc
summary: She was burned and later canonised.

name: Rana Pratap
summary: Fought at Haldighati in 1576.

name: Chand Bibi
summary: She defended Ahmadnagar in 1595.

name: Rani Abbakka Chowta
summary: She resisted Portuguese attacks for decades.

name: Lachit Borphukan
summary: He defeated the Mughals in 1671.

name: Ahilyabai Holkar
summary: She restored temples and ruled wisely.

name: Toussaint Louverture
summary: A former slave who led the only successful slave revolution.

name: Simón Bolívar
summary: He freed Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia and Panama.

name: Velu Nachiyar
summary: She recaptured Sivaganga in 1780.
